sections.h2: Your options for a fast Deer Park sale
sections.html:
Three routes are open to you: hire an agent, handle the sale yourself, or accept an offer from someone who buys the house in its present condition. The trade is usually speed against price. Refineries came to town in the 1940s and Deer Park incorporated in 1948, so plenty of streets are lined with houses from the same few decades. Shoppers for homes of that vintage look hard at slab movement, roof age and how water leaves the lot.

Put your paperwork together first: the deed, your lender's payoff number, recent tax statements and anything showing permitted work. Then lay the offers side by side. The useful ones name a closing date, say which side pays title charges and describe the condition the buyer expects at handover.

  • Find out if the buyer's offer hinges on an inspection or on loan approval.
  • Settle who pays recording and title fees.
  • Do not accept a date or a dollar figure that is only spoken.

Building, electrical, mechanical and plumbing permits each lead to inspections, and all four finals must pass before the city releases a gas meter inspection. Deer Park promises an inspection within 72 hours of a request.

Inspection stages by trade, City of Deer Park
TradeInspection stages
BuildingFoundation, frame, clip and strap, brick tie, flat work, wall cover, ceiling cover, piers, final, storm drain final
ElectricalT-pole, wall cover, ditch cover, TCI or service, ceiling cover, final
MechanicalCeiling cover, rough in, wall cover, final
PlumbingGround, water test, sewer test, top out or cover, gas test, shower pan, irrigation, final

Give the office at least a day of notice. Monday visits get called in on Friday. Morning appointments run about 8:30 to 11:30 a.m., and afternoon ones about 1 to 4 p.m. For foundation approval the city wants a form survey and an elevation certificate.

sections.h2: A permit with no final inspection
sections.html:
An unfinished permit file can stall a sale, and it can delay a utility hookup for whoever buys next. Think about the patio cover, the water heater swap or the sprinkler system someone added years ago. Irrigation appears among the city's plumbing inspections, which means an older sprinkler system may have left a paper trail at city hall.

If you find a permit that was never closed, say so to the buyer early and phone the inspection office to learn what it would take. It is cheaper in time to sort this out before you sign a contract than in the weeks between contract and closing.

Begin with permits, then turn to the lot. Pull the records for each remodel and look for work that never got a final.

  • Collect inspection stickers or approval records for recent projects.
  • Repair visible drainage, roof and fence trouble.
  • Report broken city property, such as potholes or damaged benches, through the online form on the city home page.
  • Ask neighbors or the city about street or utility work on the way, including the advanced metering project listed for residents.

Repairs you can document help every kind of buyer, and they let a cash buyer price your house with fewer guesses. A neat folder of receipts, permit numbers and final inspection dates also cuts down the questions from the title company and the lender in the last stretch. Send anyone asking about school attendance zones to the school district, because the city does not draw them.

The city's fiscal year runs October 1 to September 30. The appraised value is locked in as of January 1, and bills go out around October 1. Whatever is still unpaid after January 31 is delinquent, and penalty and interest start to build. A collector may agree to a payment plan of up to 36 months for a homestead.

Your Harris County bill carries the real numbers. The city, the county and the school district each set a separate rate. Because the lien for the year attaches on January 1 and follows the house, the balance gets paid at the closing table or cleared beforehand, and your title company will confirm the figure on closing day.

Every school district exempts $140,000 of a homestead, and other taxing units may add a local exemption of their own. Owners who are seniors or disabled receive an extra $60,000 school exemption plus a ceiling on school taxes. A homestead's appraised value can rise no more than 10 percent a year. The usual filing deadline is before May 1. The Harris County appraisal district can tell you which local exemptions apply inside Deer Park.

sections.h2: Inherited property or a loan in default
sections.html:
After a death, heirs have four years to take a will through probate. If the owner recorded a transfer on death deed while alive, the house passes with no probate at all. When there is no will and the estate is modest, a small estate affidavit may do the job. The Harris County Clerk can say what papers a sale needs.

A mortgage lender generally has to wait until a loan is more than 120 days behind. The borrower then gets 20 days to cure. Notice of the sale is posted three weeks or more ahead of a first-Tuesday auction. If you close before that day, the loan is paid off on terms you control. Ask your servicer for the payoff and the auction date.

The Harris County Clerk records your deed, and the signature must be notarized or witnessed before the clerk will take it. The title company normally files for you and pays the recording fee out of the closing funds.

A cash sale leaves out the lender's appraisal and loan approval. What remains is the title search, payoff of any current loan, the tax settlement and the signing. Bring a photo ID to the table, along with keys, garage openers and warranty papers for work done on the house.

faqs.q: Does Deer Park inspect a house when it sells?
faqs.a: Inspections are tied to permits for building, electrical, mechanical and plumbing work, not to the sale itself. Confirm that earlier permits were closed out, and call the inspection office if you are unsure about your address.

faqs.q: Who records the deed for a Deer Park house?
faqs.a: The Harris County Clerk records it, but only after the signature is notarized or witnessed. Your title company usually files it and takes the fee from closing funds.

faqs.q: Can a Deer Park house be sold with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The lien dated January 1 stays with the property, so the balance is paid at closing or cleared before it. The title company lists the amount on a payoff statement.

faqs.q: Who sets the tax rate on a Deer Park house?
faqs.a: Each taxing unit sets its own, so a single house carries several rates. The county and the school district mail separate bills, and the city posts its own rate on its home page.

faqs.q: What if a Deer Park permit never got a final inspection?
faqs.a: Tell the buyer and ask the inspection office what it needs. An open permit can slow a sale or a hookup, since all four trade finals must pass before the gas meter inspection is released.
